OrbitControls import path changed to a relative local module for subdirectory hosting.
Fonts use the operating system's installed fonts; no font service is contacted.

PLANET DATA (rounded educational values)
NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics:
https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/phys_par.html
https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html
https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sats/phys_par/
https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/astro_par.html
NASA NSSDC planetary/satellite factsheets:
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/

ROTATION AND AXIAL TILT
Positive sidereal period magnitudes with full 0-180 degree obliquity; the
tilt already encodes retrograde spin for Venus and Uranus (no double reversal).
NASA planet factsheets and definitions:
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/fact_notes.html
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html
Sun: representative 609.12 h at about 16 degrees latitude; differential rotation
is not modeled. Giant planets use representative internal rotation periods.
Saturn: 10 h 33 m 38 s, Cassini ring-seismology estimate (2019):
https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/scientists-finally-know-what-time-it-is-on-saturn/
Uranus: 17 h 14 m 52 s, Hubble estimate (2025):
https://science.nasa.gov/missions/hubble/hubble-helps-determine-uranus-rotation-rate-with-unprecedented-precision/
All 20 selected moons use ideal synchronous spin based on NASA factsheets:
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/joviansatfact.html
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/saturniansatfact.html
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/uraniansatfact.html
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/neptuniansatfact.html
Satellite poles are simplified to zero tilt, with no libration or calibrated
surface longitude. Axial azimuths and initial orientations are illustrative.
Sunlight direction is modeled, but inverse-square brightness, shadows/eclipses,
ring illumination and differential atmospheric rotation are not modeled.

FLIGHT MODEL
Ideal heliocentric Hohmann transfer between circular coplanar orbits.
Educational reference:
https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/edu/resources/lesson-plan/lets-go-to-mars-calculating-launch-windows/

TEXTURES
Sun, Mercury, Venus atmosphere, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Earth and Earth clouds:
Solar System Scope / INOVE, CC BY 4.0.
Original: https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/
License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Unmodified source pixels, rendered with 3D lighting and color adjustment.
Earth distributed in Three.js examples: https://threejs.org/examples/textures/planets/earth_day_4096.jpg
Other Solar System Scope files mirrored by TanvirAhmedArnab/SolarSystem:
https://github.com/TanvirAhmedArnab/SolarSystem/blob/main/Docs/Legal/ThirdPartyAssets.md
Earth clouds: Solar System Scope 2k_earth_clouds.jpg, via the same credited mirror.

Moon: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, CGI Moon Kit.
https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/4720/
https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/vis/a000000/a004700/a004720/lroc_color_2k.jpg

Mars: Viking / NASA / JPL / USGS, cylindrical planetary map.
https://maps.jpl.nasa.gov/tmaps/mars.html
https://maps.jpl.nasa.gov/tmaps/pix/mar0kuu2.jpg

Jupiter: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute, Cassini cylindrical map PIA07782.
https://science.nasa.gov/photojournal/cassinis-best-maps-of-jupiter-cylindrical-map/

Saturn: Solar System Scope 2k_saturn.jpg, CC BY 4.0, via the same credited mirror.

Other moons use simple illustrative colors, not surface maps.
Stars, atmospheric glow, rings, and trajectories are illustrative 3D geometry/shaders.
All scale, model and motion limitations are available in the in-app guide.
